result.topic_en: Euler rewrites the series for the column-buckling problem in terms of the dimensionless variable t = b^3/m, reduces the condition to P + PQ' − QP' = 0 in t alone, infers that the maximal heights of columns vary as the cube root of a quantity (subtriplicate ratio), and begins setting out the four series P, P', Q, Q' to be evaluated.
result.transcription:
) 182 (

§. 29. Quo nunc has formulas propius ad calculum accommodemus, ponamus $\frac{x^3}{m} = \frac{b^3}{m} = t$, atque series, quibus indigemus, sequenti modo designemus, posito scilicet vbique $x = b$:
$p = b\left(1 - \frac{1.\,t}{2.\,3.\,4} + \frac{1.\,4\,t^2}{2.\dots.7} - \frac{1.\,4.\,7\,t^3}{2.\dots.10} + \text{etc.}\right) = b.\,P$
$q = -1\left(\frac{t}{2.\,3} - \frac{1.\,3\,t^2}{2.\dots.6} + \frac{1.\,3.\,6\,t^3}{2.\dots.9} - \text{etc.}\right) = -1.\,Q$
$\int p\,dx = b^2\left(\frac{1}{2} - \frac{t}{2.\dots.5} + \frac{1.\,4\,t^2}{2.\dots.8} - \frac{1.\,4.\,7\,t^3}{2.\dots.11} + \text{etc.}\right) = -b^2.\,P'$
$\int q\,dx = -b\left(\frac{t}{2.\,3.\,4} - \frac{1.\,3\,t^2}{2.\dots.7} + \frac{1.\,3.\,6\,t^3}{2.\dots.10} - \text{etc.}\right) = -b\,Q'.$
Quod si iam istos nouos valores introducamus, postrema nostra aequatio sequentem induet formam:
$bb\,P + bb\,P\,Q' - bb\,Q\,P' = 0,$
at per $bb$ diuisa fit $P + P\,Q' - Q\,P' = 0$, quae aequatio nullam aliam literam inuoluit nisi $t$, vnde ergo si definire licuerit hanc quantitatem $t$, erit $b = \sqrt[3]{m\,t}$, hoc est $t$ [?] $= \sqrt[3]{b\,b\,e\,t} =$ altitudini columnae quaesitae; vbi valor $t$ est numerus quidam absolutus, ex illa aequatione eruendus. Quare cum $e$ pro eadem materia, ex qua columnae conficiuntur, eundum retineat valorem, pro variis amplitudinibus columnarum maximae altitudines quaesitae sequuntur rationem subtriplicatam altitudinum, id quod egregie conuenit cum theoremate dissertationi praecedenti annexo.

§. 30. Vt igitur ista altitudo $b$ per calculum definiri possit, sequentes quatuor series, quantitatem incognitam $t$ inuoluentes, rite euolui debebunt:
$P = 1 - \frac{1.\,t}{2.\,3.\,4} + \frac{1.\,4.\,t^2}{2.\dots.7} - \frac{1.\,4.\,7.\,t^3}{2.\dots.10} + \text{etc.}$
$P' = \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1.\,t}{2.\dots.5} + \frac{1.\,4.\,t^2}{2.\dots.8} - \frac{1.\,4.\,7.\,t^3}{2.\dots.11} + \text{etc.}$
Q =

items.english: For various widths of columns, the sought maximal heights follow the subtriplicate (cube-root) ratio of the heights [sic], which agrees excellently with the theorem appended to the preceding dissertation.

items.english: So that this height b can be determined by calculation, the following four series involving the unknown quantity t must be properly evaluated.
